label: prop:silver-ratio-beta-decay-null
title: **Silver-ratio trace degeneracy**: at $q = 1 \pm \sqrt{2}$, the Hecke generator $\sigma$ has eigenvalues = $1 \pm \sqrt{2}$ (silver-ratio self-referential fixed point); proton and neutron Markov-traces become categorically indistinguishable
html:
Let q be the substrate parameter, h = q - q^{-1} the Hecke skein parameter, and \mathfrak{E}_\times(q) = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) = h/2 the per-crossing energy. Then:

\boxed{\;
\Delta(\mathrm{net})
\;=\;
\frac{h(h-2)}{2}
\;=\;
\frac{(q^2-1)(q^2 - 2q - 1)}{2q^2}
\;=\;
2\,\mathfrak{E}_\times\!\left(\mathfrak{E}_\times - 1\right)
\;}

vanishes if and only if h \in \{0, 2\}, equivalently if and only if

\mathfrak{E}_\times \in \{0, 1\},

that is, if and only if each crossing carries either zero or unit energy. The two roots are q = 1 (undeformed substrate, \mathfrak{E}_\times = 0) and q = 1 + \sqrt{2}, the silver mean (unit crossing energy); the conjugate root q = 1 - \sqrt{2} is negative and outside the substrate range.

The crossing-energy form is equivalent to the h-form by \mathfrak{E}_\times = h/2. Its roots \{0, 1\} are the fixed points of x \mapsto x^2.

At q = 1 + \sqrt{2}:

  1. The Hecke quadratic \sigma^2 = h\sigma + 1 becomes \sigma^2 = 2\sigma + 1. The generator \sigma has eigenvalues equal to the silver-ratio conjugates themselves.
  2. Proton and neutron single-wrap Markov traces become equal: \mathrm{net}(p) = \mathrm{net}(n) = 1 - h/2 = 1 - \mathfrak{E}_\times = 0.

Behaviour of the mass formula at the two roots. The volume term carries \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} in the denominator as \mathrm{Vol}/\hbar_q^{2}. At \mathfrak{E}_\times = 0, i.e. q = 1, that denominator is zero. At \mathfrak{E}_\times = 1 it equals (1 - (1+\sqrt2)^{-1})^2 = 0.343\ldots, and item 2 above states that the trace does not separate proton from neutron there.

Relation to the volume conjecture. The volume-conjecture limit is taken at roots of unity q = e^{2\pi i/N}, for which |q| = 1, whereas \mathfrak{E}_\times = 1 gives |q| = 1 + \sqrt{2}. The limit in which the volume term equals the hyperbolic volume is q \to \infty, where \hbar_q \to 1 and \mathrm{Vol}/\hbar_q^{2} \to \mathrm{Vol}.
